summary: TAP proves that a key from a payment scheme's store signed this host and path, for a stated purpose, within 8 minutes. Everything else is trust placed in a party: Visa's non-public onboarding and its key store, the verifier's choice to keep nonces, and the merchant's handling of personal data. The minimum signature leaves the method, the query and the body unbound, body objects have no defined canonicalization (the specification says only: all fields in the order received). The JWKS the specification named until October 2026 holds no key that matches its examples. As of 2026-10-19 no CVE or GitHub advisory names TAP and no attack paper on it was found on arXiv; the threats below come from reading the specification and the sample code.

threats.title: Stolen agent signing key
threats.description: An attacker who obtains an Agent Provider's private key signs requests that verify as a trusted agent, browsing or paying.
preconditions: Access to the agent's key material
The key is still in the key store
threats.impact: Requests from the attacker pass every TAP check; merchants extend agent-level trust to them.
threats.implementerNotes: TAP specifies no revocation list or key status endpoint; removal from the key store or expiry is the only stop. Merchants should combine TAP with other signals and cache keys briefly.

threats.title: Method, query or body changed under a valid signature
threats.description: The minimum signature covers only @authority and @path. An intermediary can change the method, the query string or the body, including the signed objects' transport, without breaking the header signature.
preconditions: An attacker on the path or a misbehaving intermediary
The verifier relies on the minimum covered set
threats.impact: A browse-tagged signature can be reused against other methods or bodies on the same path until it expires.
threats.implementerNotes: Ask agents to cover @method, @query and Content-Digest as extra fields; verify body objects separately; keep windows short.

threats.title: Replay inside the 8-minute window
threats.description: A captured signed request is resent while it is still valid.
preconditions: The attacker can observe or obtain a signed request
The verifier keeps no nonce record
threats.impact: The replay is accepted as a trusted agent request.
threats.implementerNotes: TAP makes nonce tracking conditional. Keep nonces for at least 8 minutes, shared across edge nodes, and record them only after the signature verifies.

threats.title: Consumer data exposed to every merchant visited
threats.description: The consumer object carries IP address, device data, country and postal code, plus obfuscated contact values, to each merchant the agent visits.
preconditions: The agent attaches agenticConsumer while browsing
threats.impact: Profiling and cross-site tracking of the consumer; data protection duties for merchants.
threats.implementerNotes: The specification has no minimization or retention rule; agents should send the object only where needed and merchants should treat it as personal data.

threats.title: Credential hash with no stated salt may reveal card data
threats.description: The payment credential hash covers a 16-digit account number, expiry and a 3-digit code with no stated algorithm or salt, so the input space is small.
preconditions: The attacker sees a payment container with a credential hash
The hash is a plain digest
threats.impact: Card data could be recovered by trying candidate values.
threats.implementerNotes: Treat the hash as sensitive card data, protect it in transit and logs, and ask Visa for the algorithm and any salt.

threats.title: Unverified consumer data used for decisions
threats.description: The specification lets a merchant use consumer recognition data even when verification fails.
preconditions: The merchant follows the discretionary wording
An attacker forges an agenticConsumer object
threats.impact: Account matching or risk decisions based on forged identity data.
threats.implementerNotes: Use consumer data only after the nonce and signature verify; never log a user in on unverified data.

threats.title: Key store confusion
threats.description: The JWKS the specification named until October 2026 held one RSA key from a sandbox CA and no Ed25519 key. Visa's own code uses that key for MCP token encryption, so verifiers may source keys elsewhere or accept keys loosely.
preconditions: The verifier cannot resolve the agent's keyid from the JWKS the specification named until October 2026
An out-of-band key path is used
threats.impact: Keys from an untrusted path could be accepted as Visa's.
threats.implementerNotes: Accept keys only from a channel Visa documents; pin the key store origin; alert on unknown keyids.

threats.title: Key store or verification as a single point of failure
threats.description: Every verification needs Visa's key store or a cached key; an outage or a CDN error blocks agents at many merchants at once.
preconditions: Key cache expired during an outage
threats.impact: Legitimate agents blocked; merchants fall back to bot rules.
threats.implementerNotes: Cache keys with a reasonable lifetime; the JWKS the specification named until October 2026 uses a one-hour cache-control; monitor fetch failures.

threats.title: No receipt or evidence from TAP
threats.description: TAP defines no receipt, so a verified request leaves no portable evidence of what the agent was allowed to do.
preconditions: A dispute about an agent purchase
threats.impact: Disputes rest on VIC signals and card rules, not on TAP records.
threats.implementerNotes: Log verification results with the signature parameters; rely on VIC confirmations for transaction evidence.

threats.title: Interoperability gaps bypass verification
threats.description: Sample code builds non-RFC signature bases, uses an unregistered algorithm name, and its CDN proxy protects only /product/ paths, skipping the tag and window checks. Implementations copied from it can be bypassed.
preconditions: A deployment reuses the sample code
threats.impact: Checkout and API paths left unverified; old or mis-tagged signatures accepted.
threats.implementerNotes: Use a conformant RFC 9421 library, verify every path that matters, and check the tag and window explicitly.

threats.title: browsingIOU without settlement terms
threats.description: The merchant grants access on a signed IOU expecting funds at settlement, but TAP defines no settlement or default rule.
preconditions: The merchant serves paid content against IOUs
threats.impact: Unpaid access with no protocol remedy.
threats.implementerNotes: Limit IOU amounts and exposure per agent; agree settlement terms with the payment service and acquirer.

scenarios.title: A browse signature reused against checkout data
preconditions: The attacker captures a browse-tagged request to a path that also accepts POST
The verifier checks only the minimum components
steps: The attacker copies Signature-Input and Signature
Within 8 minutes it sends a POST to the same host and path with its own body
The header signature verifies because method and body are not covered
A verifier without a nonce record accepts it
scenarios.impact: Requests with attacker-chosen content inherit trusted agent status.

scenarios.title: Card data recovered from a credential hash
preconditions: A payment container with paymentCredentialsHash is logged or leaked
The hash is an unsalted digest
steps: The attacker learns the card's bank identification range and expiry candidates
It hashes candidate numbers and security codes
It finds the input that matches the hash
scenarios.impact: Usable card data for card-not-present fraud.

scenarios.title: A sample-code edge lets checkout through unchecked
preconditions: A merchant deploys the sample CDN proxy
steps: The proxy verifies only paths starting with /product/
An attacker posts directly to the checkout path
No signature is required and rate limiting is off
scenarios.impact: Bot traffic reaches checkout as if it had passed the agent gate.

research.title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
research.finding: Argues that the Visa and Mastercard network agent protocols, along with MCP, A2A, x402 and AP2, assume rather than produce a determination of whether an agent met its obligation. Its full text names Visa's TAP, as do the GLEIF working paper, the Visa and Artemis report and a 2026-10-16 arXiv white paper.

research.title: A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols
research.finding: Models x402, MPP, ACP and AP2 in Tamarin; TAP is not modeled, and no formal analysis of TAP was found (arXiv search, 2026-10-19).

research.title: FP-Inconsistent: Measurement and Analysis of Fingerprint Inconsistencies in Evasive Bot Traffic
research.finding: About half of the traffic bought from 20 bot services evaded two commercial anti-bot products by altering browser fingerprints, the weakness that signed agent requests aim to replace.

research.title: Verified by Visa and MasterCard SecureCode: Or, How Not to Design Authentication
research.finding: Criticizes 3-D Secure for unverifiable password frames and for shifting liability onto cardholders; a reference point for any network-run authentication layer.
